coverage.authentication: Actual Firebase Auth/Firestore emulators and the existing FirebaseAuth implementation; upstream phone verification and SMS delivery are synthetic.
accountConfigurations: Accepted caretaker without an owned phone
Accepted caretaker who also owns a different phone
coverage.resourceHeaderChecks: Direct audio and durable delivery deny access with no selected-person header or with the caretaker own-person header.
coverage.dataProof: The owner reads the exact synthetic private summary and audio bytes. Saved/shared contacts are created through the API.
coverage.separateConsent: History-only and explicit listening access are granted and revoked through the API. Caretaker decline preserves an independent sharing grant; sharing revocation preserves caretaker consent.
coverage.deletion: API-created accepted caretaker erased; former ID/refresh tokens rejected; same-phone recreation uses a new UID without old consent or audio access; protected owner and message preserved.

retainedIssues: Initial two account failures were positive-control failures: the synthetic owner lacked an enrolled Shield number. The fixture was completed; no production guard was weakened.

Default Firestore startup found port 8089 occupied by Java process 53288. That process was preserved; the same npm target and test selection ran using an ignored isolated configuration on port 8388, hub 8480 and logging 8481.

MetadataLookupWarning is retained in the account/database logs. The installed gcp-metadata source emits it from its metadata-service availability probe and returns unavailable. No warning was suppressed.
limitations: Emulator identities do not prove signed production-token validation, production IAM, actual SMS/APNs delivery or physical-device revocation.
This checkpoint changes tests and evidence only; live account erasure and vendor/other-device deletion remain unverified.
The six-hour healthy snapshot and policy enablement do not establish actual alert-condition delivery, failure recovery, all deployed package hashes or historical incident causes.
Native request metrics may arrive late; the six retained API 401 responses are not individually attributed.
The database retry rollout, Apple work, physical calls, full accessibility and other release gates remain open.
